subject: A better way to model errors?

messages.author: 263bab466ba6e11b
messages.subject: A better way to model errors?
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I would be grateful for thoughts on the following issue. 

Suppose I want to have a set exogenous variables to all be uncorrelated. Is there a way to easily do this? 

1. I realize that I can fix the covariances I want to zero within the model syntax, but this can be a little tedious doing that variable by variable (for many exogenous variables that I don't want correlated). 

2. I also realize that I can use "orthogonal = TRUE" in, say, sem() to have *all* of the exogenous variables uncorrected (and allow specific correlations by explicitly specifying them in the lavaan syntax), but this doesn't seem ideal either. 

I'm wondering if there is an easy way to say in the syntax something that means "don't correlate these variables with anything else." 

Here is the context: suppose I create named errors for the variables so that I might, for example, model the errors directly. Take a simple three factor Holzinger and Swineford example. If I create named errors 
(done as follows for x1):
E_x1 =~ 1*x1
x1 ~~ 0*x1 

I would have to specify the following:

visual ~~ 0*E_x1 + 0*E_x2 + 0*E_x3 + 0*E_x4 + 0*E_x5 + 0*E_x6 + 0*E_x7 + 0*E_x8 + 0*E_x9  
textual ~~ 0*E_x1 + 0*E_x2 + 0*E_x3 + 0*E_x4 + 0*E_x5 + 0*E_x6 + 0*E_x7 + 0*E_x8 + 0*E_x9
speed ~~ 0*E_x1 + 0*E_x2 + 0*E_x3 + 0*E_x4 + 0*E_x5 + 0*E_x6 + 0*E_x7 + 0*E_x8 + 0*E_x9 

E_x1 ~~ 0*E_x2 + 0*E_x3 + 0*E_x4 + 0*E_x5 + 0*E_x6 + 0*E_x7 + 0*E_x8 + 0*E_x9
E_x2 ~~ 0*E_x3 + 0*E_x4 + 0*E_x5 + 0*E_x6 + 0*E_x7 + 0*E_x8 + 0*E_x9
E_x3 ~~ 0*E_x4 + 0*E_x5 + 0*E_x6 + 0*E_x7 + 0*E_x8 + 0*E_x9
E_x4 ~~ 0*E_x5 + 0*E_x6 + 0*E_x7 + 0*E_x8 + 0*E_x9
E_x5 ~~ 0*E_x6 + 0*E_x7 + 0*E_x8 + 0*E_x9
E_x6 ~~ 0*E_x7 + 0*E_x8 + 0*E_x9
E_x7 ~~ 0*E_x8 + 0*E_x9
E_x8 ~~ 0*E_x9

So, specifically, is there a better way to accomplish specifying a set of exogenous variables to be uncorrelated? If not, might a "mutually uncorrelated" option be useful? 

Also, is there a better way to incorporate named errors into a model than that demonstrated above for E_x1? Perhaps a way that specifies named errors but yet doesn't correlate them with anything?

Thanks for any thoughts on this,
Ken

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: A better way to model errors?
parts:
On 07/03/2014 04:49 PM, kke...@nd.edu wrote:
> Suppose I want to have a set exogenous variables to all be uncorrelated.
> Is there a way to easily do this?
If you are looking for an option/argument for doing this automatically: no.

> 1. I realize that I can fix the covariances I want to zero within the
> model syntax, but this can be a little tedious doing that variable by
> variable (for many exogenous variables that I don't want correlated).

But this is R! You can easily 'generate' (parts of) model syntax. It is
just generating strings. For example:

HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

vis <- paste0("visual ~~ ", paste0("0*E_x", 1:9, collapse = " + "))
txt <- paste0("textual ~~ ", paste0("0*E_x", 1:9, collapse = " + "))
spd <- paste0("speed ~~ ", paste0("0*E_x", 1:9, collapse = " + "))

ortho <- apply(combn(9,2), 2, function(x)
paste0("E_x", x[1], " ~~ ", "0*E_x", x[2]))

errors <- paste0("E_x", 1:9, " =~ 1*x", 1:9, "; x", 1:9, " ~~ 0*x", 1:9)

and then, you glue them together:

fit <- cfa( c(HS.model, errors, vis, txt, spd, ortho),
data=HolzingerSwineford1939)

> 2. I also realize that I can use "orthogonal = TRUE" in, say, sem() to
> have *all* of the exogenous variables uncorrected (and allow specific
> correlations by explicitly specifying them in the lavaan syntax), but
> this doesn't seem ideal either.

What about the lavaan() function? Only the parameters you specify in the
model syntax will be estimated. Everything else is fixed to zero.

So, the above syntax would simplify to:

HS.model <- ' visual =~ 1*x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ 1*x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ 1*x7 + x8 + x9
visual ~~ textual + speed
textual ~~ speed '

errors <- paste0("E_x", 1:9, " =~ 1*x", 1:9, "; x", 1:9, " ~~ 0*x", 1:9)

fit <- lavaan(c(HS.model, errors), auto.var=TRUE,
data=HolzingerSwineford1939)

> I'm wondering if there is an easy way to say in the syntax something
> that means "don't correlate these variables with anything else."

No. Perhaps I could add a new operator. Something like

var1 + var2 + var3 + var4 ~~ 0

but we do not gain much.

Yves.

messages.author: 263bab466ba6e11b
messages.subject: Re: A better way to model errors?
parts:
Hi Yves,

Thanks for the reply. 

You mentioned the possibility of using R to generate parts of model syntax for a situation like I described. I think that is not ideal, as it gets messy. Using the lavaan function instead of SEM would work, provided I specified (at least in the case here), "auto.fix.first=TRUE" (I like how in sem() the path of the first manifest variable for each factor is automatically set to 1). 

I actually *really like* the idea of a new operator that would translate into words as "all of these variables are mutually uncorrelated", like the possible code "var1 + var2 + var3 + var4 ~~ 0" you mentioned. 

Similarly, I think an operator that would translate into words as "correlate all of these variables" would be useful too, like "var1 + var2 + var3 + var4 ~~ NA"

Thanks for your reply and your work on lavaan, 
Ken
